routes.description: Establish that objective moral value, categorical obligation, responsibility, and moral knowledge require a transcendent personal ground that theism supplies and secular humanism does not.
routes.successCriteria: Show that God explains the existence, authority, and human apprehension of moral facts while secular goal-based norms remain conditional on interests that agents may reject.

motionBridge.description: God must provide a more adequate foundation for ethics than secular humanism by grounding objective value, categorical duties, and reliable moral cognition.

centralBridges.description: Objective moral properties and obligations must require a nonphysical ground capable of conferring value and authority.
Theism must connect human moral faculties to moral truth rather than merely explain their causal origin.
The secular account must fail to bind agents who reject human well-being or benefit from exceptions to cooperative norms.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Creation in God's image must supply a basis for human worth, rights, and restraints on harming others.
Theistic belief may support the route by supplying conduct-guiding recognition of objective human worth and obligation.

routes.description: Establish that secular humanism supplies a usable, evidence-responsive ethical framework based on human interests, consequences, cooperation, and correction without requiring divine moral facts.
routes.successCriteria: Show that shared conditions of social life support objective means-end judgments and revisable public norms, while a generic or disputed God adds no demonstrated ethical content or dependable access.

motionBridge.description: Secular humanism must provide a more usable and supportable foundation for ethics than an unspecified and undemonstrated divine ground.

centralBridges.description: Human needs, interests, and interdependence must provide a sufficient starting point for ethical concern and cooperation.
Observable consequences must permit non-subjective judgments about which actions better advance human well-being.
Evidence, reason, empathy, and revision must provide methods for identifying error and improving social norms.
The God proposal must lack demonstrated normative content, stable interpretation, or an inference from divine existence to particular duties.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Unchosen participation in social life must explain why individual indifference does not prevent collective ethical judgment and intervention.
Relationships, empathy, and mutual dependence must support human value without requiring cosmic or intrinsic value.

sectionSelections.title: Moral reality and the content of a foundation
sectionSelections.rationale: The comparison centrally depends on whether objective moral phenomena require a divine ground and whether invoking God supplies ethical content rather than merely naming an entity.

proSelections.proposition: An adequate moral foundation must account for objective obligations, intrinsic value, responsibility, and moral improvement rather than redefine those phenomena.
Theism explains nonphysical moral properties and human access to them by grounding goodness and authoritative obligations in a creator.

conSelections.proposition: An unspecified God is an entity rather than an ethical system, and disagreement about divine identity and aims prevents it from furnishing usable ethical principles.
Invoking an unspecified creator does not establish objective moral truths or duties and therefore does not itself supply a foundation for ethics.

sectionSelections.title: Categorical obligation and goal-based normativity
sectionSelections.rationale: A principal burden clash concerns whether ethical requirements must bind independently of chosen ends or can arise from shared interests, social participation, and factual consequences.

proSelections.proposition: Goal-dependent ethics cannot bind people who reject universal well-being and can generate instrumental requirements for vicious goals rather than genuine moral duties.
Identifying effective means to human well-being does not establish a moral obligation for an agent who rejects human flourishing as a goal.

conSelections.proposition: People who share concern for human well-being can assess actions non-subjectively by their real consequences for achieving a better human life.
People participate in consequential social life without choosing to enter it, and physical facts can establish better outcomes despite an individual's indifference.

sectionSelections.title: Moral knowledge, error, and correction
sectionSelections.rationale: The rival foundations must explain how moral beliefs connect to truth or justified practice and how mistaken judgments can be detected and corrected over time.

proSelections.proposition: On a non-theistic evolutionary and social account, moral beliefs track survival or conditioning rather than moral facts, undermining confidence that moral cognition is truth-directed.
Theism can explain fallible but reliable moral knowledge through God-given faculties, whereas evolutionary or social causes of belief do not make those beliefs objectively true.

conSelections.proposition: Mistaken conceptions of well-being can be exposed through internal conflict, observable consequences, and evidence without abandoning well-being as the ethical standard.
Secular humanism uses empathy, education, evidence, and revision to pursue better outcomes without assuming an undemonstrated objective imperative or divine enforcer.

sectionSelections.title: Human value and moral motivation
sectionSelections.rationale: The comparative routes also depend on whether theism uniquely supports human worth and restraint or whether human relationships and public methods supply adequate reasons for ethical conduct.

proSelections.proposition: Wood's conversion is presented as evidence that belief in objective God-given human worth can transform conduct where naturalistic descriptions did not motivate restraint.

conSelections.proposition: A belief that restrains one person is not thereby a better foundation than a public humanist method grounded in shared goals, evidence, reason, and human needs.
Human value need not be cosmic or intrinsic because interdependence, empathy, and cooperation support valuing people while allowing reasonable differences in personal priority.

sectionSelections.title: Divine grounding, specificity, and circularity
sectionSelections.rationale: The theistic route must distinguish metaphysical grounding from a religious ethical code while addressing whether identifying God with goodness demonstrates or merely assumes the proposed standard.

proSelections.proposition: God can be the necessary standard and ground of moral goodness independently of whether Christianity is the ethical system under discussion.

conSelections.proposition: A generic deity supplies no ethical system, while reliance on specifically Christian commands shifts the case from abstract theism to a disputed religious framework.
Defining God as the standard of goodness is circular and does not demonstrate that objective moral facts possess a divine foundation.
